Losar (Tibetan New Year)

A Home Celebration of Losar: Tibetan New Year

Welcome the Tibetan New Year, Losar, with a day of renewal, reflection, and delicious traditional foods right in your home. This agenda brings ancient customs into a modern setting for a meaningful celebration.

  1. Morning

    Renewing Prayer Flags

    Begin the day by replacing old prayer flags with new ones, symbolizing fresh hopes and blessings for the year ahead. If you don't have flags, a simple cleaning of your home altar or sacred space can serve a similar purpose.

  2. Late Morning

    Crafting Khapse Pastries

    Gather your family to prepare deep-fried khapse pastries. These beautiful, symbolic treats are a hallmark of Losar, offering a sweet start to the new year.

    Recipes: Deep-Fried Khapse Pastries

  3. Midday

    Connecting with Tradition

    While visiting monasteries isn't possible, take time to watch videos of cham dances or listen to Tibetan Buddhist chants. This connects you to the spiritual heart of Losar and its ancient observances.

  4. Afternoon

    Sharing Auspicious Wishes

    Share white khata scarves (or any symbolic gesture of purity and goodwill) with family members, reciting auspicious wishes for health, happiness, and prosperity in the coming year.

  5. Late Afternoon

    Warmth and Welcome

    Prepare and share warm butter tea, a staple of Tibetan hospitality, perhaps alongside some dried yak cheese or your freshly made khapse, embodying the spirit of community.

    Recipes: Tibetan Butter Tea (Po Cha) · Prepared Dried Yak Cheese (Chhurpi) · Deep-Fried Khapse Pastries

  6. Evening

    The Symbolic Feast

    The highlight of the evening is enjoying guthuk noodle soup. Prepare the dough for the symbolic dumplings, each holding a different meaning, and share this special meal with loved ones, reflecting on the year past and the year to come.

    Recipes: Guthuk Noodle Soup · Losar Guthuk (Tibetan Symbolic Dumpling Soup)

May your Losar be filled with joy, peace, and renewed hope for the year ahead!
